tasks.short: Instruct patients and families in home skills and adaptive equipment

steps.what: Read the therapist's home programme and equipment instructions
Demonstrate basic living skills and safe care of adaptive equipment
Coach patients and families through practice and check understanding
Prepare the actual home instruction sheet from the prescribed programme
Check final home instructions against the prescription and intended recipient
Hand the checked home instruction sheet to the patient or family

tasks.design: Configure a {DOCS} home-instruction template with reusable headings and equipment-care sections. The assistant selects only prescribed content, enters individual details, demonstrates skills and checks the final sheet before physically handing it to the patient or family.
tasks.previous_blocker: Practical instruction is personal, while handout layout and standard care sections can repeat.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates can reuse layout and already approved equipment-care text without choosing treatment.
tasks.still_hard: Equipment fit, comprehension and safe use must be checked with the patient.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant adapts demonstrations to what the patient and family can actually do.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less handout assembly; instruction and treatment authority are unchanged.

evidence.claim: Native document templates can reuse headings and selected standard text; this is model knowledge, not measured occupational therapy instruction savings.

assumptions: Boundary includes an actual home sheet used between visits, not a new routine lesson log. Verbal-only instruction has no invented paperwork.

The therapist produces the programme's activity, frequency, equipment and precautions. The assistant reads it in s1, asks about gaps within retained instruction time and first enters patient-specific sheet details in s4. No structured programme feed is assumed.

Test native templates first. Two of ten preparation hours are repeated layout and standard care text; eight remain for selecting, entering and checking the individual instructions. Ordinary author saves stay in those eight hours with no gate or saving.

The four-hour final check follows writing and gates only physical delivery of that exact sheet to the intended recipient. Changes invalidate the check. Performance observations and clinical reporting are explicitly handled in 4256 and 4262, not silently bundled into teaching.
unknowns: Whether existing home sheets already use templates
Which equipment-care sections are approved for reuse
research_questions: How much actual handout assembly remains after using native templates?

already_counted.description: First enter individual instructions and check the final sheet against the programme

incremental.description: Maintain template layout and approved equipment-care sections

approvals.approved_version: Exact home instruction sheet and patient or family recipient checked in s5; edits require another check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: two assembly hours removed less 0.4 upkeep gives 1.6. Cautious case: a bespoke adaptive device needs unique instructions or the current sheet already supplies all layout; all ten preparation hours remain and no additional template is maintained. Demonstration, practice and delivery remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Listen to clients' concerns about themselves and their treatment programmes
Maintain and promote a positive attitude toward clients and treatment

tasks.design: Keep supportive therapeutic interaction with the assistant. No {OTHER} clinical-record automation is added to this attitude task; actual performance capture and supervisor reporting are separately decomposed in 4256 and 4262.
tasks.previous_blocker: Positive attitude is expressed in how the assistant listens and responds.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology removes an identified action in this interaction.
tasks.still_hard: Clients can feel discouraged or mistrust treatment and need a personal response.
tasks.human_edge: Respect, patience and consistent encouragement build the therapeutic relationship.
tasks.altitude: No change to this part of the week or to decision rights.

reach.task: Support patients who are discouraged during care

evidence.claim: A positive therapeutic interaction depends on the assistant's conduct; this is model knowledge, not a claim about an automated intervention.

assumptions: Boundary is listening and the assistant's general therapeutic stance, rather than task-specific performance coaching in 4256. The two are distinct actions for this decomposition; a roll-up must avoid counting the same live interaction twice if observed together.
The client provides concerns during the interaction; there is no assumed structured sentiment feed, conversation recording or administrative input contract.

Checking for actual paperwork identifies performance first capture in 4256 and the real supervisor report and send in 4262. No new attitude rating, conversation summary or trailing engagement record is invented here.
A native-software check reveals no repeated record handling within these two actions. No additional tool means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: How general support and activity-specific coaching overlap in observed sessions
research_questions: Can observed time distinguish general therapeutic support from activity coaching without double counting?

already_counted.description: Listen and respond supportively to client concerns

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All one hundred hours of listening and supportive interaction remain. Actual performance recording and supervisor communication have their own decompositions; no write or send is hidden here. No new upkeep is introduced.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Report patient progress, attitudes and behaviour to supervisors

steps.what: Read existing performance entries and identify relevant progress changes
First enter additional attitude and behaviour facts needed for the report
Copy existing patient, session and measured performance fields into the report
Write the patient progress, attitude and behaviour report

loop.purpose: Draft only the supported progress narrative
loop.input: Dated source fields and assistant-entered factual brief
loop.output: Source-linked draft report with gaps left explicit
loop.check: Assistant compares every progress and behaviour statement with the actual observations, checking clinical meaning and correcting omissions
loop.stop: Missing or conflicting observations return to manual writing; no unsupported interpretation or diagnosis
loop.why_not_simpler: Report headings and exact field copies are configurable; varying observations need prose that a fixed template cannot assemble reliably

steps.what: Check the final report's clinical meaning and supervisor recipient
Send the checked progress report to the supervisor
Discuss patient progress and clarify the supervisor's questions verbally

tasks.design: Test the {OTHER} clinical-record system's native report fields and supervisor notification first. Reuse existing measured entries, retain first capture of new behavioural facts, and use a bounded draft only for narrative; the assistant checks final meaning and recipient before a separate real send, while verbal clarification remains intact.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress reporting combines repeated source fields, new observations and narrative that cannot be trusted without clinical checking.
tasks.enabler_now: Native field reuse and notifications can be combined with a narrowly grounded narrative draft.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle changes and the difference between observation and inference require the assistant's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant knows the patient and can explain uncertainty or unexpected behaviour to the supervisor.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated field copying and report prose; reporting responsibility and supervisor decisions remain the same.

reach.task: Report treatment response to the supervising therapist
reach.learn: Source-linked progress description and clear uncertainty

evidence.claim: Exact field reuse and source-grounded narrative drafts are technically plausible; this is model knowledge. The digest's physiotherapy intake capability does not demonstrate occupational therapy progress-report savings.

assumptions: Boundary includes the actual written supervisor report and its verbal clarification. It does not add a new report to verbal-only cases; that branch keeps its conversation time.

The assistant creates patient identifier, session date, activity, observed performance and assistance level in 4256 s3. This task reuses those already captured facts without claiming their capture again. Additional attitude and behaviour facts not in those entries are first entered here in s2.
Field reuse requires matching patient and session identifiers plus source dates. Missing fields are manually resolved within s1, s2 and s5; no free structured observation feed is assumed.

Native fields and report templates are tested first. Ten repeat-copy hours and ten narrative hours are removed; fifteen narrative review/edit hours and fourteen final-check hours remain. Ordinary same-system author saving is retained inside writing and has no gate.
Only the actual supervisor notification is gated. The final report and exact supervisor destination must exist before s5; any change invalidates the send approval.
unknowns: Whether the system already reuses all source fields
How much prose needs individual rewriting
research_questions: Can every draft progress statement be traced to a dated observation without adding assumptions?

already_counted.description: First capture additional facts, review generated prose and check final clinical meaning

incremental.description: Review draft errors and maintain source mappings and notification permissions

approvals.approved_version: Exact final patient progress report and supervisor recipient checked in s5; edits require rechecking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: ten field-copy hours, ten prose hours and one actual-send hour removed, less two upkeep hours, gives 19. Cautious case: a complex behavioural account needs all twenty-five narrative hours, but matching source fields still remove ten copy hours and the real send removes one; less two upkeep gives 9. First capture and verbal discussion remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor therapy performance and encourage patients

steps.what: Monitor patients' performance and assistance needs during therapy activities
Encourage the patient with cues matched to the observed activity
First enter and verify the measured therapy performance in clinical records
Save the author's verified performance entry

tasks.design: Keep direct monitoring and activity-specific encouragement with the assistant. Configure native patient and session defaults in the {OTHER} clinical-record system, while retaining first entry and verification of actual performance and the ordinary author save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Performance must be seen directly, though entry can repeat the already selected patient and session context.
tasks.enabler_now: Native encounter defaults can remove repeated context fields without generating clinical observations.
tasks.still_hard: Pain, fatigue, unsafe movement and discouragement need immediate human interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant adjusts encouragement to the patient's real performance and comfort.
tasks.altitude: Almost no change to the therapy session; only repeated context entry may shrink.

reach.task: Observe and record patient performance during treatment
reach.learn: Consistent performance measures and safe assistance cues

evidence.claim: Native encounter defaults can supply existing identifiers while the assistant enters observations; this is model knowledge, not automated therapy monitoring evidence.

assumptions: Boundary includes direct observation, specific performance cues and first capture of measures actually used by the therapist and the supervisor report in 4262. No new surveillance or engagement log is introduced.

The assistant produces activity, measured performance, assistance level and relevant observed response during s1 and first enters them in s3. The existing clinical-record encounter provides patient identifier and date; missing context is entered manually within retained time.

Test native encounter defaults first. Only 0.7 of seven entry hours is repeated patient and session context; 6.3 hours of first observation capture and verification remain. The one-hour same-system author save is fully retained and ungated.

General supportive attitude in 4255 is distinct from activity-specific performance cues here. Where observed interactions overlap, a team roll-up must resolve ownership rather than add the same live action twice. The actual supervisor report and send are priced in 4262.
unknowns: Whether context fields are already supplied
Which measures are actually recorded during sessions
research_questions: Does the current encounter view already eliminate repeated context typing?

already_counted.description: First enter and verify the actual observed performance measures

incremental.description: Check encounter field defaults after system changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: 0.7 repeated-context hours removed less 0.1 upkeep gives 0.6. Cautious case: the encounter screen already supplies patient and session fields, so all eight record hours remain and no extra configuration is maintained. All ninety-two monitoring and encouragement hours remain in either case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Practical instruction, encouragement and monitoring still dominate. Native templates and source-linked supervisor reporting may remove a small amount of preparation and repeated documentation.
reach: Physical therapist assistant: improve home instruction and supervisor handover
Nursing assistant: strengthen supportive patient communication
skills_to_grow: Consistent observation capture and source checks
Native clinical forms and recipient-bound reporting
role.ambitious_version: An assistant whose reports are easier to check while hands-on instruction and the therapeutic relationship remain personal work.
